# Contribution Guidelines

**30 seconds of code** is supported by the community, so feel free to contribute in any way you can to help!

## How you can help

- Submit Issues or Pull Requests related to bugs, improvements, typos etc.

## Ground rules

Breaking any of these rules will result in your pull request being closed. Please follow these guidelines above all else:

- **Always be polite and respectful to others** and try to follow the advice of the maintainer.
- **Only modify files under the `content/snippets` or `content/collections` directories**, when making changes to the website content (i.e. bug fixes or improvements).

## Writing guidelines

All content on the website should follow the guidelines below. These guidelines are not exhaustive, but they should be followed as closely as possible.

### Language

- Use words and language that our audience understands.
- Use American spelling for all content.
- Write short sentences (ideally 20 words or less).
- Make sure each sentence has a single focus.
- Edit unnecessary or repeated words.
- Avoid idioms and phrases with indirect or ironic meanings.
- Avoid jargon and overly technical terms.
- Aim for a Grade 10 reading level or below.
- Use contractions to create a natural voice, but don’t overdo it with contractions that are hard to pronounce or aren’t used often.
- Conversely, not using a contraction can be used to add emphasis.
- Directional language (e.g. “above”, “below”) may only be used as part of a piece of content to indicate a relevant section of the content (e.g. “the above code example”).
- Prefer non-directional language if possible. Replace “above” and “below” for section indication with “previous” and “following”.

### Voice

- Prefer writing in an active voice wherever possible.
- Avoid writing in a passive voice.
- Prefer a passive voice if you want to emphasize the action instead of the subject, clarify that an action wasn’t taken by a certain person or to avoid referring to the subject (i.e. the 30 seconds of code team or yourself).
- Use imperative voice when documenting code snippets (e.g. “use this method”).
- Don’t use permissive language (e.g. “you can use this method”).

### Capitalization

- Capitalize the first letter of a sentence, lowercase the rest.
- Keep the original capitalization of terminology (e.g. "JavaScript"), acronyms (e.g. "CRUD"), products (e.g. "GitHub Actions") or trademarks (e.g. "Netlify") anywhere they’re used on the website.

### Punctuation

- Avoid ampersands (&), as they focus attention in the wrong part of the sentence. Spell out the word “and” instead.
- Use apostrophes to represent omitted numbers or letters, contractions or to form possessives.
- Use quotation marks to define words or quoted text.
- Avoid using periods in the middle of sentences, unless it’s inside an inline code block or part of a term (e.g. "Node.js").
- Use colons in the middle of sentences sparingly.
- Use a colon to preface a list.
- Use periods only to finish full sentences.
- Use question marks sparingly. Try rewording to an affirmative if possible.
- Do not use the oxford comma (also known as the serial comma) in sentences.
- Don’t use commas to separate bulleted or numbered list items.
- The ellipses (...) can be used in place of a missing piece of text. Avoid using ellipses in regular text, use them only in headings.
- Avoid exclamation marks as much as possible. If you really have to use one, limit them to one per page.
- Avoid semicolons if possible. Try replacing them with a comma, the word “and” or splitting the sentence in two separate sentences.
- Use hyphens without spaces for ranges.
- Use hyphens in place of regular dashes inside a sentence with a space on either side.
- Use hyphens to form compound modifiers.

### Terminology

- Use terminology sparingly and only when necessary.
- Only use industry-standard or well-established terminology.
- Explain terms if you’re not sure the reader understands them.
- Link to any relevant content on the website, if possible.

### Emphasis

- Use bold sparingly to highlight important information on the page.
- Don’t use bold to create a heading.
- Use italics to quote text, usually in the form of short verbatim phrases.
- Use quotation blocks for longer sentences when you want to draw particular attention to them. Limit yourself to one quotation block per page.

### Dates

- Use the American English format for dates ({month} {date}, {year}).
- Use the 3-letter abbreviation for months, followed by a period.
- Do not add nominal suffixes to date numbers.
- Don’t write dates numerically.

### Code

- Wrap inline code blocks in the appropriate visual element.
- Wrap important values to the code such as numerals, strings or boolean values in the appropriate visual element.
- Use multiline code blocks wherever the code spans more than one line.
- Provide appropriate language context and highlighting to multiline code blocks.
- Use the full name or the name that’s closest to the official documentation when describing native code (e.g. "Function.prototype.apply()").
- Do not use code blocks in headings.

### Personal pronouns

- Use “I” or “my” for personal opinions, experiences or when you want to express your personal voice.
- Use “we” or “our” when referring to the 30 seconds of code team.
- Use “we” or “our” when the audience is supposed to be following along and you want to sound reassuring.
- Use “you” or “your” when explaining something to the audience and you want to sound authoritative.

### Headings

- Capitalize the first word of a heading, lowercase the rest if the heading is formatted as a sentence.
- You may capitalize the first letter of each word if the heading is not formatted as a sentence.
- Avoid using punctuation such as periods, commas, colons or semicolons.
- Headings may use a question mark if the content is a question-type article.
- Keep headings short. Avoid headings that are longer than one line.
- Limit headings to a single sentence. The only exception to this is headings that span multiple short questions.
- Headings need to be informative and descriptive.
- Avoid clickbait-type headings.
- Use headings that help the user understand what they’ll find in the related content.
- Use headings to make content easier to scan.
- Use a hyphen surrounded by a single space on either side for articles that are part of a series.
- For tip-type articles, start the heading with the word “Tip” followed by a colon and a space.
- Omit articles such as “the”, “a” and “an” in regular headings if possible.
- Omit articles such as “the”, “a” and “an” in microcopy.
- You can use ampersands (&) in microcopy headings to make the heading shorter.

### Lists

- Use bulleted (unordered) lists wherever possible.
- Use numbered (ordered) lists for listicles or sequences of steps.
- Prefer bulleted lists over numbered lists for documenting code snippets.
- List items should start with a capital letter in all cases.
- Don’t use commas or semicolons at the end of list items.
- If any list item contains two or more sentences, punctuate all list items.
- If all list items are one sentence or fragments, don’t punctuate.
- Use bulleted lists to make content easier to scan.

### Actions

- Actions should lead with a strong verb when possible (e.g. “Search”, “View all”).
- Capitalize the first word of an action, lowercase the rest.
- Label links in a predictable way.
- If a link leads to a page with its own heading (e.g. Snippet, Article or Collection), prefer using the original heading of the content.
- Links in full sentences should be applied only to the relevant text, not the entire sentence.
- Links in full sentences must be descriptive, either on their own or based on their surrounding context.

### Alternative text

- Provide alternative text for visual content whenever possible.
- Use empty alternative text for decorative visual content.
- Alternative text should help users navigate the site and provide an accessible experience.

# 30 seconds of code

> Coding articles to level up your development skills

* Visit [the website](https://30secondsofcode.org) to view all articles.
* Search for articles and collections that suit your needs, using the name, tags, language or description.
* Browse all [articles](https://30secondsofcode.org/snippets/p/1) or individual [collections](https://30secondsofcode.org/collections/p/1) for each topic.
* Click on each card to view the whole article, including code snippets, explanation and examples.
* If you like the project, give it a star. It means a lot.

## Want to contribute?

* New content contributions are not accepted at this time.
* You can, however, report problems with the website or suggest improvements by [opening an issue](https://github.com/Chalarangelo/30-seconds-of-code/issues/new).

## Credits

* This repository is maintained by [Angelos Chalaris](https://github.com/Chalarangelo).
* All code snippets are licensed under the [CC-BY-4.0 License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), unless explicitly stated otherwise.
* Any other material (including text content, images, the website source code, logos, names and trademarks) are not to be used without the explicit consent of the owner.
* The website is powered by [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com/), [Astro](https://astro.build/) & [GitHub](https://github.com/).
* All of the photography is provided by [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/collections/9387655/30-seconds-of-code-images).

report.overview: 30-seconds-of-code is the source for the statically-generated website www.30secondsofcode.org, an Astro 6 site that publishes a large library of short-form coding articles ('snippets') organized into YAML-defined collections. It is distinctive in that almost everything is custom-built: a bespoke content pipeline (bin/prepare) parses Markdown front-matter and YAML into a .content/content.json intermediate, hydrates an in-process ActiveRecord-style model layer, serializes page payloads to JSON files that Astro routes consume via getStaticPaths, and ships a hand-rolled TF-IDF + trigram-fuzzy search engine that runs both at build time and in the browser. Deployment is a scheduled GitHub Actions job that simply curls a Cloudflare build hook.

system_map.summary: The system is a two-phase static site generator: bin/prepare transforms content/ Markdown and YAML into .content/ JSON artifacts, then astro build renders pages whose getStaticPaths read those JSONs. A custom model layer (Model/RecordSet), page adapters, and serializers mediate between raw content and Astro routes. Client interactivity is a few vanilla JS scripts (omnisearch, hotkeys, toc) loaded via <script src> in Astro components — there are no framework islands. Hosting is static (Cloudflare build hook triggered from GitHub Actions), and tests run under Vitest against spec/ fixtures.

claims.claim: Astro is configured with srcDir 'src/astro', site https://www.30secondsofcode.org, compressHTML, and inlineStylesheets 'always'.
bin/prepare is the build orchestrator CLI with commands: full, dev, content, watch, assets, create, create-component, help.

npm scripts wire preparation into lifecycle hooks: predev/prebuild run bin/prepare (dev/full), dev/start run 'astro dev --port 8000', build runs 'astro build', test runs 'vitest', console runs bin/console.
The project is pure ESM ('type': 'module'), requires Node >=22.14.0, and uses '#src/*' and '#spec/*' subpath imports mirrored in jsconfig paths.

A custom in-process data layer exists: Model keeps static instances/indexedInstances/getterCache registries, caches getters via WeakMap redefinition, and exposes all/where/order/scope/find/search class APIs.
RecordSet extends Array with where (equality, array-membership, or predicate functions), order, pluck, shuffle, first/last — it is the query primitive used by every model scope.
The model registry is exactly five classes: ContentModel (abstract base), Collection, CollectionSnippet (join model), Language, Snippet.
Loader.importData reads .content/content.json and hydrates model instances through a JSON.parse reviver keyed on each record's 'model' discriminator field.

Page adapters form a registry: Page.register stores classes by name and Page.from(object) resolves the adapter as `${object.constructor.name}Page`; PageSerializer emits {params, props} where props includes structuredData (schema.org JSON-LD).
AstroContent.generate writes three JSON artifacts consumed by Astro routes: .content/pages/index.json, [lang]/[...listing].json, and [lang]/s/[snippet].json.

The search stack is hand-rolled and shared between build and browser: server.js tokenizes content into 'token:count' strings, DocumentIndex builds term + trigram inverted indexes, and documentSearch scores with TF-IDF blended with n-gram similarity.

Deployment is a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (cron '20 18 * * *' plus workflow_dispatch) that executes bin/deploy, a bash script that POSTs to a Cloudflare build hook URL stored in the CF_BUILD_HOOK_URL secret.
Client-side behavior is delivered by three plain scripts referenced from components via <script src>: omnisearch.js (search modal), hotkeys.js (keyboard nav), toc.js (table of contents).
Generated artifacts live in gitignored paths: .content/, src/astro/timestamp.js, public/search-data.json, public/sitemap.xml, public/feed.xml, public/_redirects, public/components.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing features are all static pages and client widgets: a home page, paginated collection listing pages, snippet article pages, an about page and 404, plus an omnisearch modal, keyboard shortcuts, RSS feed, sitemap, and redirects file. Content-level features (collections, journeys, article embeds, admonitions, codepen embeds, automatic code-reference links, table of contents) are produced by the custom markdown pipeline. Author-facing features include snippet/collection scaffolding commands, a watch mode, an interactive REPL console, and an asset pipeline that resizes cover images.

claims.claim: Snippet pages at /{lang}/s/{snippet} are rendered by [snippet].astro with breadcrumb, snippet content, journey prev/next pagination, a 'More like this' recommendation list, a table-of-contents sidebar, and a content-components fallback.
Paginated listing pages are served by [lang]/[...listing].astro, which reads .content/pages/[lang]/[...listing].json and renders a Hero, optional sublink Chips, a PreviewList, and Pagination.

The home page composes a Hero, an optional Announcement banner (latest update-log snippet within the last 30 days), featured collection Chips (top 7 plus an 'Explore collections' link), and a PreviewList of the 12 newest published snippets.

The omnisearch modal lazily fetches /search-data.json on first open, builds a DocumentIndex in the browser, searches on keyup (queries of 1 char or less are ignored), supports ArrowUp/ArrowDown result navigation, and closes on Escape, backdrop click, or the close trigger.
Keyboard hotkeys bind Ctrl/Cmd+k to omnisearch, Ctrl/Cmd+j to collections, and Ctrl/Cmd+h to home, with Mac detection via navigator.userAgent.

Collections are YAML-defined and populated three ways: explicit snippetIds lists, languageMatcher/tagMatcher filters, or the special 'snippets' main collection which ranks all snippets; 'collections' hub gets featured ordering from hub.yaml featuredListings.

Journeys are multi-part articles: a snippet's journeyId front-matter links it to a Collection, and Snippet.journeyPagination computes previousUrl/nextUrl/url/title/itemNumber for the Pagination component.

Article embeds: '<article-embed ref="..." title="..."/>' markup in rendered content is replaced at read time by Snippet.enrichedContent with an asEmbedding figure produced via ContentModel.searchContentModels.

The markdown pipeline applies remark plugins (highlightCode, embedCodepensFromLinks, transformArticleEmbeds) then HAST plugins (loadWebComponents, linkInlineCode, safeguardExternalLinks, transformAdmonitions, transformHeadings for h2-h4 with linkable ids, transfomImagePaths, wrapTables) before rehype-stringify.
linkInlineCode auto-links inline code tokens to language reference URLs (e.g. MDN) declared in content/languages/*.yaml 'references' and 'additionalReferences' maps.

SEO features: each Page emits schema.org JSON-LD (TechArticle for snippets, ItemList for collections, WebSite for home), Snippet.seoTitle prefixes the language name when absent from the title, and ContentModel.seoDescription strips HTML for meta descriptions.

Build-time outputs for the site include an RSS feed (public/feed.xml), a sitemap listing home/about/snippets/all collection pages, and a Netlify-style _redirects file generated from content/redirects.yaml.

The asset pipeline (prepareAssets) uses sharp to convert content/assets/{cover,splash} images into sized .webp variants in public/assets — covers at 800x400/400x200/1200x600 and splashes at 600x600/400x400 — and copies static 'icons' and 'illustrations' directories.

Content web components are supported: scripts under content/components/scripts are copied and SCSS under content/components/styles is compiled to public/components; the loadWebComponents HAST plugin injects <script type=module> tags when markup references them.

Authoring commands: 'bin/prepare create [snippet|collection] [dir] [name]' scaffolds content from content/collection-template.yaml or per-directory snippet-template.md files, filling title/slug/dateModified; 'bin/prepare create-component' scaffolds components; 'bin/console' opens a REPL with all models and PreparedQueries preloaded.

data_flow.summary: Data flows one direction: content/ sources → extraction (FileHandler globs + front-matter/YAML parsing) → per-model workers that render HTML, tokenize, rank, and build join records → .content/content.json → in-memory model graph via Loader reviver → page adapters + serializers → .content/pages/*.json plus public/ artifacts (search-data.json, feed.xml, sitemap.xml, _redirects) → Astro getStaticPaths → static HTML. The browser is a terminal consumer: it fetches search-data.json and rebuilds the same DocumentIndex used at build time. There is no runtime server state; 'state owners' are the static Model registries hydrated once per build/console process.

claims.claim: Input boundaries are globbed files: content/snippets/**/s/*.md (front-matter + markdown), content/collections/**/*.yaml, content/languages/*.yaml, plus singleton files grammars.yaml, rankingEngine.yaml, hub.yaml — all read through FileHandler.read which dispatches on extension to JSON/YAML/front-matter readers.

extractData is the single orchestration point: it loads languages, grammars, hub, and keyword data; selects Shiki or Prism as codeHighlighter; calls MarkdownParser.setupProcessors and sets Ranker.keywordScores; then extracts snippets, collections, and collectionSnippets in that order.

Snippet extraction derives id from filePath by stripping the 'content/snippets/' prefix and '.md' suffix, renders excerpt and body to HTML through a per-language MarkdownParser processor, computes recTokens and docTokens via tokenize(), computes a 0-1 ranking via Ranker.rankIndexableContent, and builds tableOfContentsHtml via TocReader when tocEnabled.

MarkdownParser maintains one unified() processor per language short-code plus a 'default'; each processor embeds that language's reference map (merged from allLanguageReferences) for linkInlineCode, so inline-code autolinking is per-language.

exportXData functions flatten extracted objects into plain records tagged with a 'model' field ('Snippet', 'Collection', 'Language', 'CollectionSnippet'); ContentUtils.prepareContent writes the aggregate to .content/content.json via FileHandler.write.

CollectionSnippet join records are produced by extractCollectionSnippetData: explicit snippetIds are looked up with a console.warn on missing, matcher-based collections filter ranked snippets by languageKey/tags, the 'snippets' main collection gets position = rank index (-1 for unlisted), and allowUnlisted controls inclusion.

On load, every model constructor pushes itself into Model.instances[name] and registers each declared index into Model.indexedInstances[name][index] maps; all Snippet and Collection instances are indexed on 'id'.

Page serialization path: AstroContent.generate calls Collection.pages / snippet.page / Page.home, each Page subclass exposes params and props getters, PageSerializer.serialize emits {params, props:{...props, structuredData: schemaData}}, and results are keyed by page.key into JSON files under .content/pages/.

Astro routes are pure consumers of generated JSON: [snippet].astro and [...listing].astro implement getStaticPaths by reading the corresponding .content JSON file and mapping entries to {params, props}; index.astro reads index.json synchronously at module scope.

Search data path: snippet/collection docTokens strings ('token:count' space-joined) are serialized by SearchResultSerializer into public/search-data.json; the browser fetches it, deserializeTokens rebuilds Map<term,freq>, and DocumentIndex re-derives trigram sets for fuzzy matching.
Ranker scores content against the sorted keyword table from content/rankingEngine.yaml, capping at 20 keywords or a score of 100, and returns max(0.0001, score/100) so no snippet ranks exactly 0.

Redirects flow: content/redirects.yaml is loaded once in a static block, Redirects.generate writes 'from to status' lines to public/_redirects, and Redirects.for(slug) does a transitive lookup used by ContentModel.allSlugs for canonical/alias handling.

TimestampDump.generate writes a hex timestamp to src/astro/timestamp.js, which Layout.astro injects via define:vars into an empty script solely to force HMR when content regenerates during watch mode.

behavior_traces.summary: The three flows worth knowing end-to-end: (1) 'npm run dev' runs the content pipeline with Prism fast-highlighting then starts astro dev; (2) 'npm run build' runs the full pipeline (assets + Shiki + all generated artifacts) then astro build; (3) at runtime, the only dynamic behavior is the omnisearch modal which fetches the prebuilt search index. A fourth flow — watch mode — respawns the whole dev pipeline per file change, and deployment is a cron-triggered Cloudflare webhook call.

claims.claim: Dev startup trace: npm run dev → predev 'bin/prepare dev --fast-highlight' → sets NODE_ENV=development → ContentUtils.prepareContent('prism') → extractData → FileHandler.write(.content/content.json) → Loader.loadModules + importData → AstroContent.generate → SearchIndex.generate → TimestampDump.generate → ContentComponents.prepare → 'astro dev --port 8000'.

Full build trace: npm run build → prebuild 'bin/prepare full' → ContentUtils.prepareAssets (sharp image conversion, non-forced) → prepareContent with Shiki (fastHighlight=false) → importData → AstroContent.generate → SearchIndex.generate → Redirects.generate → Feed.generate → Sitemap.generate → TimestampDump.generate → ContentComponents.prepare → 'astro build'.

Watch trace: 'bin/prepare watch [--fast-highlight]' → FileWatcher.watch does fs.watch('content', {recursive:true}) → every event logs the filename and exec()s a fresh 'bin/prepare dev' child process — a full re-extraction per change with no debounce.

Snippet page render trace (at astro build): getStaticPaths reads .content/pages/[lang]/s/[snippet].json → each serialized SnippetPage entry supplies params {lang, snippet} and props {breadcrumbs, pageDescription, snippet(context), journey(pagination), recommendations(collection+snippets, ≤4 previews)} → Layout renders Breadcrumb, SnippetContent, Pagination (if journey), PreviewList, ContentComponentsFallback, TableOfContents.

Recommendation trace inside a snippet page build: SnippetPage.props reads object.recommendedSnippets → RecommendationPresenter.recommendSnippets() scores candidates pre-grouped by languageId and primaryTag (language up to 45 pts, primary tag up to 15, recToken overlap up to 40, thresholds per settings.recommendations) → top results merged with recommendedCollection and sliced to 4 previews.

Omnisearch runtime trace: user clicks [data-open-modal] → open() → prepare() fetches /search-data.json once → documents mapped {id:url, content:deserializeTokens(searchTokens)} → new DocumentIndex → search(index) closure → keyup on #omnisearch → searchByKeyphrase trims/lowercases, returns [] for len<=1 → searchDocuments(q,100) → TF-IDF term scoring + 0.7-weighted ngram similarity → displayResults writes innerHTML list.

Scheduled publishing trace: snippet front-matter dateModified in the future → Snippet.isScheduled true → Snippet.scope('published') excludes it; AstroContent.generateSnippetPages uses Snippet.all when NODE_ENV==='development' but Snippet.scope('published') otherwise, so scheduled articles appear locally but not in production builds.

Deploy trace: deploy-production.yml runs on cron '20 18 * * *' or manual dispatch → checkout@v1 → chmod +x ./bin/deploy → './bin/deploy production' → bash curl -X POST to $DEPLOY_URL (secret CF_BUILD_HOOK_URL) with trigger_title and trigger_branch=master → Cloudflare rebuilds and serves the static site.

Content creation trace: 'npm run create' → 'bin/prepare create snippet js my-name' → ContentCreator.create resolves content/snippets/js/snippet-template.md as the template → replaces title and dateModified (today) via regex → mkdirs content/snippets/js/s if needed → writes my-name.md; collections similarly use content/collection-template.yaml with slug/name replacement.

Console trace: 'npm run console' → bin/console starts node:repl → Loader.loadModules + importData hydrates the full model graph → models/serializers/pages/module classes injected into REPL context → PreparedQueries functions bound and documentIndex prebuilt → exposes helpers like searchForTerm, snippetsWithoutFormatting, snippetCoverUsage.

testing_signals.summary: Tests are Vitest specs under spec/, mirroring src/ structure: core, models, presenters, and lib/contentUtils. Coverage is real but selective — model logic, presenters, ranker, tocReader, stringUtils, search utils, metaParser, and an integration-style prepareContent test against fixture content. Factories (base + named traits) are the fixture mechanism, built through Loader.buildFactories. CI runs 'npm ci && npm test' on Node 22.14 for pushes and PRs to master. Notable gaps: no specs for serializers, page adapters, documentIndex/documentSearch/porterStemmer, assetHandler, extractor end-to-end, or any Astro/client code.

claims.claim: 'npm test' runs bare 'vitest' (no config file found at repo root); CI invokes the same command on Node 22.14.0 for push/PR to master.

Spec layout mirrors src/: spec/core (model, serializer), spec/models (collection, contentModel, snippet), spec/presenters (breadcrumb, cover, recommendation, sublink), spec/lib (contentUtils, ranker, tocReader, stringUtils, search/utils, metaParser).

The fixture mechanism is factory objects: spec/factories export {model, base, traits} and Loader.buildFactories() composes base + named traits + inline overrides, then news up the registered model class.

spec/lib/contentUtils/contentUtils.test.js is an integration test: it vi.mocks the config module to point at spec/fixtures/content and FileHandler.write to capture output, then runs the real ContentUtils.prepareContent and asserts output keys and language objects.

spec/fixtures/content is a miniature of the real content tree — snippets (js/css/articles), collections (js/css/webdev), languages (js/css/html), grammars.yaml, hub.yaml, rankingEngine.yaml — letting the pipeline run end-to-end without touching real content.

snippet.test.js demonstrates the shared-global-state pattern: Loader.loadModules() and Factory.create() calls run at describe scope, registering instances into the process-global Model.instances registry — meaning tests are implicitly order/isolation sensitive.

Coverage gaps: no spec exists for serializers/*, adapters/*, lib/search/documentIndex.js, documentSearch.js, porterStemmer.js, extractor.js, assetHandler.js, astroContent.js, or any src/astro code — the .content/pages JSON contract and the browser search index have no automated tests.

Linting is eslint 9 flat config (js.configs.recommended + eslint-config-prettier) with a custom globals.js file; style rules enforce single quotes, semicolons, multiline comma-dangle, as-needed arrow-parens; prettier + prettier-plugin-astro via .prettierrc. No lint or format check runs in CI.

Other workflows are maintenance automation only: stale.yml marks inactive issues/PRs via actions/stale@v5 and label.yml applies path-based PR labels via actions/labeler@v4 — neither runs tests or builds.
There is no coverage tooling, no e2e/browser test, and no build-verification step in CI — the 'test' job is the only quality gate and it never runs 'astro build' or 'bin/prepare full'.

risk_map.summary: Top risks: production code imports test factories (spec/ is on the live path of bin/console and any Loader user); the model layer is global mutable state; the markdown pipeline passes through raw HTML (allowDangerousHtml) so content is trusted input; watch mode has no debounce; omnisearch injects index data into innerHTML; and several identifiers are derived by brittle string slicing/naming conventions. Deploy security hinges on a single secret webhook URL, and CI is thin (tests only, old action versions, no build check).

claims.claim: src/lib/loader.js imports '#spec/factories/factories.js' — test-only factory code is imported by a production module, coupling any Loader user (bin/prepare, bin/console) to the spec tree.

Model state is process-global and append-only: Model.instances accumulates every constructed instance with no reset API, so double importData calls or tests that create factories leak records into all/where/scope results for the process lifetime.

The markdown pipeline runs remark-rehype and rehype-stringify with allowDangerousHtml:true — raw HTML embedded in snippet markdown passes through unescaped into shipped pages; safe only because all content is author-trusted.

omnisearch renders result rows via innerHTML template literals interpolating result.url, result.title, result.tag without escaping (createResultHTML), while only the not-found path escapes the query — a crafted search-data.json title could inject markup, though the index is build-generated.

Watch mode exec()s a full 'bin/prepare dev' on every fs.watch event with no debounce or in-flight guard — rapid saves can spawn overlapping full re-extractions (Shiki highlighting is the expensive step).

Snippet id derivation is positional: filePath.replace(snippetPrefix,'').slice(0,-3) assumes the 'content/snippets/…/*.md' shape; a stray file matched by the glob with a different extension would silently corrupt the id.

A missing/typo'd front-matter 'language' degrades silently: languageData.get(languageKey) returns undefined and every downstream use is optional-chained, so recTokens/docTokens lose language terms and the snippet renders without a language rather than failing.

Naming-convention coupling is load-bearing: Page.from resolves `${object.constructor.name}Page`, serializeAs resolves `${name}Serializer`, and the JSON reviver resolves models[value.model] — renaming a class or key breaks page generation, and the 'serializer not found' guard in serializeAs is dead code because `new undefined()` throws TypeError first.

Publishing correctness depends on wall-clock time: dateModified compared to new Date() decides scheduled vs published, so the daily 18:20 UTC deploy cron determines when scheduled articles go live — a missed/failed deploy silently delays publication.

Astro routes hard-fail without generated content: getStaticPaths does fs.readFile on .content JSONs with no fallback, so 'astro dev'/'astro build' without the prepare step (or a cleaned .content dir) crashes — the coupling is enforced only by npm pre-hooks, which bare 'astro' or 'vitest' invocations bypass.
Known-fragile code is flagged in TODO comments: Snippet.hasCollection returns true even when the only membership is the main collection, and Collection.matchesTag relies on id.endsWith(`/${tag}`).

CI uses dated action versions (actions/checkout@v1 in deploy-production, actions/setup-node@v1 in test) and the deploy job's only secret is CF_BUILD_HOOK_URL — a leaked or misconfigured hook URL is the entire deployment control surface.

Shiki vs Prism output differs subtly: Prism mode appends a '<script type=module …/prism-code-highlights.mjs>' tag into parsed HTML, meaning dev-mode rendered markup is not identical to production markup.

extension_points.summary: The repo is designed for extension mostly at the content layer: drop a markdown file into content/snippets/{lang}/s/, a YAML into content/collections or content/languages, and the glob-driven pipeline picks it up automatically. Code-level extension follows consistent registries and naming conventions: new models register via Model.prepare + models.js, new page types via Page.register + `${Model}Page`, new serializers via Serializer.prepare + `${name}Serializer`, and new markdown features via the remark/HAST plugin list in plugins/index.js. Search, ranking, and presentation are tuned through data files and settings rather than code.

claims.claim: New snippet: add {name}.md under content/snippets/{lang}/s/ with front-matter (title, shortTitle, language, tags, cover, excerpt, listed, dateModified, optional tocEnabled/journeyId); the content/snippets/**/s/*.md glob picks it up with zero code changes.

New collection: add a YAML under content/collections with slug, title, description, and either explicit snippetIds or languageMatcher/tagMatcher; optional parent/topLevel/listed/allowUnlisted control hierarchy and visibility; hub.yaml featuredListings controls homepage featuring order.

New language: add {name}.yaml under content/languages with short/long/name/references/additionalReferences — it is globbed automatically and its references map feeds linkInlineCode autolinking and merged additionalReferences.

New model: extend ContentModel (or Model), add a static block calling Model.prepare(this, [indexes]) and ContentModel.addContentModel(this), define scopes as static methods taking a records param, and register it in models.js so the JSON reviver can instantiate it.

New page type: create a Page subclass with a static { Page.register(this) } block, implement params and props getters, optionally additionalSchemaData — PageSerializer picks it up automatically; the class MUST be named `${Model}Page` for Page.from resolution.

New serializer: extend Serializer, declare fields via Serializer.prepare(this, [key | [key, fn], ...]), and expose it through serializers.js — ContentModel.serializeAs resolves `${name}Serializer` by name.

New markdown transform: add a plugin under plugins/ast (pre-remarkRehype, operates on mdast) or plugins/hast (post-remarkRehype, operates on hast), export it from plugins/index.js, and .use() it in MarkdownParser.setupProcessors — ordering constraints are documented inline (e.g. linkInlineCode must precede safeguardExternalLinks).

Highlighter swap/extension: ShikiHighlighter and PrismHighlighter are interchangeable via the 'shiki'|'prism' parameter selected by the --fast-highlight flag; Shiki languages are driven by content/grammars.yaml and the theme by codeHighlighters/themes/cosmos.json; custom Shiki transformers live in codeHighlighters/transformers.

Search tuning is config-driven: stop words live in src/lib/search/settings.js, token filtering rules in server.js tokenFilter, fuzzy weight is a parameter to search(), and recommendation scoring constants are in settings.js recommendations block.

Presentation is tuned in settings.js: cardsPerPage/collectionCardsPerPage, home card counts, tag display-name map, cover sizes/suffixes/srcsets, sublink labels, and collection id constants (mainCollectionId, updateLogsCollectionId, updateLogTag).

New generated artifact: write a class with a static generate() writing into settings.paths.out.* and call it from bin/prepare's full/dev command lists — Redirects, Feed, Sitemap, TimestampDump, SearchIndex, AstroContent all follow this pattern.

New client behavior: add a plain JS file under src/astro/scripts and reference it from an .astro component via <script src='../scripts/x.js'>; for reusable content widgets, drop scripts/styles under content/components and let loadWebComponents inject them into rendered HTML.

agent_handoff.summary: Conventions: ESM everywhere, #src/#spec import aliases, single quotes + semicolons + multiline trailing commas, class-static utility style, and ActiveRecord-ish model scopes. Safe edit boundary is content/ for content work (CONTRIBUTING restricts PRs to content/snippets and content/collections) and src/ for pipeline code — never edit generated paths (.content/, public/search-data.json, src/astro/timestamp.js, etc. — all gitignored). Before touching rendering, read settings.js, contentUtils/config.js, extractor.js, the modelWorkers, and the relevant model+adapter pair. Run 'npm test' (Vitest) after changes; use Loader.buildFactories in specs. Traps: global model registry, class-name coupling, scheduled-vs-published filtering differences between dev and prod, and the mandatory prepare step before any astro command.

claims.claim: Always run the prepare step before astro commands: 'npm run dev'/'npm run build' chain it via pre-hooks, but a bare 'astro dev', 'astro build', or editor-driven vitest run against a missing .content/ will crash — .content is gitignored so fresh clones must generate it.
Import style: use the '#src/…' and '#spec/…' aliases declared in package.json 'imports' (mirrored in jsconfig.json paths); the codebase is 'type': 'module' and requires Node >=22.14.0.

Code style is enforced by eslint flat config: single quotes (avoidEscape ok), semicolons, always-multiline comma-dangle (functions never), as-needed arrow-parens, 1tbs braces, plus prettier with prettier-plugin-astro — match surrounding style since CI does not lint.

Recommended read order for pipeline work: src/config/settings.js → src/lib/contentUtils/config.js → extractor.js → modelWorkers/* → src/models/* → src/adapters/page* → src/serializers/* → src/astro/pages/*.

In specs, construct records via Loader.loadModules() + Loader.buildFactories() with named traits (e.g. SnippetFactory.create('published', {id: 'x'})) — never new models directly without understanding that each construction registers globally in Model.instances.

Do not rename model classes, page adapters, or serializers: Page.from uses object.constructor.name, the content.json reviver uses the 'model' string field, and serializeAs concatenates names — renaming requires updating all three conventions at once.

Dev/prod asymmetry: NODE_ENV=development includes scheduled (future dateModified) snippets in generated pages; production excludes them — verify dateModified front-matter when a snippet 'disappears' after deploy.

CONTRIBUTING ground rules restrict content PRs to content/snippets and content/collections; content should follow the writing guidelines (US spelling, short sentences, Grade-10 level, imperative code docs) in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Use 'bin/prepare dev --fast-highlight' (Prism) for local iteration — Shiki highlighting is the slow path reserved for full builds; remember Prism mode appends a script tag to rendered HTML so markup differs slightly between modes.

Generated outputs to never hand-edit: .content/**, src/astro/timestamp.js, public/search-data.json, public/sitemap.xml, public/feed.xml, public/_redirects, public/components, public/assets — all produced by bin/prepare and listed in .gitignore.

Debugging/exploration tool: 'npm run console' opens a REPL with all models, serializers, pages, PreparedQueries functions, and a prebuilt documentIndex — the fastest way to inspect the hydrated content graph.

When editing the markdown pipeline, respect documented plugin ordering: highlightCode, embedCodepensFromLinks, transformArticleEmbeds must run before remarkRehype (mdast phase); linkInlineCode must run before safeguardExternalLinks; transformHeadings handles only h2-h4 and adds the linkable ids TocReader later matches with a regex.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working on 30-seconds-of-code (github.com/Chalarangelo/30-seconds-of-code), the source of the static website www.30secondsofcode.org. It is an Astro 6 static site, but almost none of the interesting logic is in Astro: the repo is a custom content pipeline plus an in-memory model layer.

ARCHITECTURE. Content lives in content/: snippets are Markdown with YAML front-matter under content/snippets/{lang}/s/*.md, collections are YAML under content/collections/**, languages under content/languages/*.yaml, plus singletons grammars.yaml, rankingEngine.yaml, hub.yaml, redirects.yaml. The CLI bin/prepare (commands: full, dev, content, watch, assets, create, create-component) orchestrates the build: ContentUtils.prepareContent → extractData (src/lib/contentUtils/extractor.js) → FileHandler globs + front-matter/YAML parsing → modelWorkers (snippet/collection/collectionSnippet/language) which render HTML via a per-language unified/remark/rehype pipeline (MarkdownParser), tokenize for search, and rank via Ranker → writes .content/content.json. Loader.importData then hydrates that JSON into model instances (Snippet, Collection, CollectionSnippet, Language — see src/models/, base class src/core/model.js with global instance registry and index Maps; queries via RecordSet where/order/pluck/scope). Page adapters (src/adapters/page*, resolved as `${Model}Page`) plus serializers produce {params, props} JSON written to .content/pages/*.json. Astro routes (src/astro/pages: index.astro, [lang]/[...listing].astro, [lang]/s/[snippet].astro, about, 404) read those JSONs in getStaticPaths. bin/prepare full additionally generates public/search-data.json, feed.xml, sitemap.xml, _redirects, src/astro/timestamp.js, and compiles content/components. Search is custom TF-IDF + trigram fuzzy (src/lib/search/*), rebuilt client-side in src/astro/scripts/omnisearch.js.

COMMANDS. npm run dev (chains 'bin/prepare dev --fast-highlight' then astro dev :8000), npm run watch, npm run build (full pipeline + astro build), npm test (vitest), npm run console (REPL with models + PreparedQueries). Node >=22.14, ESM, import aliases '#src/*' and '#spec/*'.

RULES/TRAPS. (1) Never run bare astro commands without the prepare step — routes read .content JSONs that are gitignored and generated. (2) Never edit generated files: .content/**, public/search-data.json, sitemap.xml, feed.xml, _redirects, components, assets, src/astro/timestamp.js. (3) Do not rename model/page/serializer classes — name-concatenation conventions resolve them. (4) Model.instances is global and append-only; in tests use Loader.buildFactories traits, and beware cross-test pollution. (5) Dev shows scheduled snippets (future dateModified); production does not. (6) Use --fast-highlight locally; Shiki is the slow production path. (7) Content PRs belong only under content/snippets or content/collections per CONTRIBUTING.md. (8) Lint style: single quotes, semicolons, multiline comma-dangle, arrow-parens as-needed. Test with 'npm test'; there is no CI build step, so verify 'bin/prepare dev' + 'astro build' manually for pipeline changes.
